sectionsContent.title: Distance, Displacement & Average Velocity

concept.summary: Distance is how far you travelled; displacement is how far you ended up from where you started. Distance is a scalar and never negative. Displacement is a vector — it carries a sign, and the sign is meaningless until you say which way is positive.
keyIdeas: Speed pairs with distance. Velocity pairs with displacement. They are not interchangeable words.
A round trip has real distance and zero displacement, so it has real average speed and zero average velocity.
State your positive direction before you write a single number.

items: Scientific notation and significant figures (U0 S0.2).
Rearranging an equation for the variable you want (U0 S0.3).
Reading a value off a number line, including negative positions.

sectionsContent.directions: Work every problem in your Hayden-McNeil notebook. Number each one, show the givens, and carry units the whole way through. Bring the sheet and your notebook to class.

questions.prompt: Spider-Man swings 5 m east across 5th Avenue, then swings 3 m farther east to land on a rooftop water tower — Aunt May still doesn't know where he's been all afternoon. Find the total distance travelled and the displacement.
questions.solution:
Total distance = 5 m + 3 m = 8 m — both legs add, direction doesn't cancel distance.
Both legs are east (positive), so displacement Δx = +5 m + 3 m = +8 m.

questions.prompt: The Batmobile covers 120 km across Gotham on a grocery run for Alfred, taking 2.0 hours because of, well, Gotham traffic. Find its average speed in km/h.
questions.solution: speed = distance ÷ total time = 120 km ÷ 2.0 h = 60 km/h.

questions.prompt: SpongeBob makes the long way round through Bikini Bottom on a Krusty Krab delivery — 90 km in 3.0 hours, because Patrick insisted on a snack break halfway. Find the average speed in km/h.
questions.solution: speed = distance ÷ total time = 90 km ÷ 3.0 h = 30 km/h.

questions.prompt: Iron Man's suit flies 200 m east from the tower, then doubles back 50 m west because FRIDAY reminds him he forgot his phone charger again. Find the total distance travelled and the displacement.
questions.solution:
Total distance = 200 m + 50 m = 250 m.
The east leg is +200 m; the west leg is opposite direction, so −50 m. Displacement Δx = 200 m − 50 m = +150 m.

questions.prompt: Batman's grappling hook yanks him from x = 10 m to x = 70 m across a Gotham alley in 20 s, while Robin yells "wait for me!" from the ground. Find the displacement and the average velocity.

Patrick Star tumbles 8 m north down a sand dune, then tumbles 8 m south back to where he started, taking 10 s total, because he forgot which way the Krusty Krab was. Find the total distance, the displacement, and the average velocity.
parts: Before you calculate: which of those three will be zero, and why?
questions.solution:
Total distance = 8 m + 8 m = 16 m.
Displacement = 0 m: he ends at the same point he started, so the two legs cancel.
v̄ = Δx ÷ Δt = 0 m ÷ 10 s = 0 m/s. Distance is never zero for a real round trip, but displacement and average velocity are exactly zero whenever the start and end points match.

questions.prompt: Aquaman swims from x = 5 m to x = −15 m along the reef in 10 s, chasing a shopping cart that fell off the pier. Find the displacement and the average velocity.

The Batmobile starts at x₀ = −15 m in the Batcave tunnel, races forward to x = 50 m, then backs up to a final position of x = 40 m, all in 25 s, because Alfred texted that dinner's getting cold. Find the total distance travelled and the average velocity.
questions.solution:
Leg 1: −15 m to 50 m, a distance of |50 − (−15)| = 65 m forward.
Leg 2: 50 m to 40 m, a distance of |40 − 50| = 10 m backward.
Total distance = 65 m + 10 m = 75 m.
Displacement Δx = x_f − x_i = 40 − (−15) = +55 m.
v̄ = Δx ÷ Δt = 55 m ÷ 25 s = 2.2 m/s.

questions.prompt: The Flash's speedometer (yes, he installed one) reads an average velocity of 3.4 m/s during a very unimpressive grocery run. Convert it to km/h and express your answer with the correct number of significant figures (U0 S0.2).
parts: Then say in one sentence why 3.4 m/s and 12.24 km/h are not equally honest answers.
questions.solution:
3.4 m/s × 3.6 = 12.24 km/h (the conversion factor 3.6 is exact and doesn't limit sig figs).
3.4 m/s carries 2 significant figures, so the reported answer must also carry 2: 12 km/h.
12.24 km/h claims four significant figures of precision that the original 3.4 m/s measurement never supported — the extra digits are arithmetic noise, not real precision. That's why it isn't an equally honest answer.
